summary: This stylesheet styles a revision history timeline component. It creates a vertical timeline with connected dots representing different revisions, where the latest revision gets special styling with a filled dot and a glowing halo. The layout uses flexbox to position content next to timeline nodes, and CSS custom properties to theme colors consistently.

explanations.9: The 'composes' syntax pulls in styles from a global 'mk-surface' class, combining them with the styles defined here — it's like inheriting styles from another class.
explanations.14: Same as line 9, but for the 'mk-eyebrow' global class, which provides base styling for this title.
explanations.27: The '::before' pseudo-element creates a fake element that exists only in CSS — here it's the vertical line connecting all the timeline dots.
explanations.32: This calculates the line height dynamically: it takes 100% of the container's height and subtracts 8px (4px from top and bottom) so the line doesn't extend past the first and last nodes.
explanations.49: Pulling in the 'mk-dot' global class which probably provides the base circular dot styles.
explanations.53: The 'z-index: 1' ensures the dot appears on top of the connecting line behind it.
explanations.62: The 'box-shadow' with 0 offset creates a glowing ring around the dot without moving it — the 4px spread makes the halo visible.
explanations.66: Setting 'flex: 1' makes the content area grow to fill remaining space in the flex container, pushing it to the right of the timeline dot.
explanations.80: The 'tabular-nums' variant makes all numbers the same width so dates line up nicely when stacked.
